parts.text:
22 Wave-power generators take advantage of the energy that is transferred by the motion of waves
across the surface of the oceans. The energy of a wave depends on its amplitude.
What is the correct definition of amplitude?
A
the average amount of energy possessed by a wave
B
the difference in displacement between a peak and a trough
C
the maximum displacement of a point on the wave from equilibrium
D
the number of oscillations of a wave that occur per second

hints: Focus on the word displacement in the options - amplitude describes how far the medium moves, not energy or rate.
Remember displacement is always measured from the equilibrium line, not from a peak to a trough.
Check which option gives a single-sided maximum from equilibrium and which options describe frequency or peak-to-trough distance.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the definition of amplitude for an ocean surface wave, where particles oscillate about an equilibrium level.
Recall the wave rule: displacement $x$ varies with time, and amplitude $x_0$ is the largest value of $|x|$ reached on either side of equilibrium.
Test the distractors: average energy describes an effect of amplitude, and number of oscillations per second describes frequency.
Note that difference in displacement between a peak and a trough is peak-to-peak height, equal to $2x_0$, so it is double the amplitude.
Therefore the maximum displacement from equilibrium matches the definition. This is option C

A.explanation: Energy depends on amplitude, but amplitude itself is a displacement, not an amount of energy.

B.explanation: Peak to trough distance is twice the amplitude, from $+x_0$ to $-x_0$, so it is not the definition of amplitude.

C.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum magnitude of displacement from the undisturbed equilibrium position.

D.explanation: Number of oscillations per second defines frequency $f$, measured in $\text{Hz}$, not amplitude.
